issues.summary: The createE2eStore doc comment now wrongly says state is shallow-cloned and that initialState can be corrupted, but the code deep-clones it.
issues.label: low
issues.evidence: createE2eStore.ts:6-7 was changed by this PR to say state is shallow-cloned, but lines 30 and 49 call deepClone(initialState), so reset() always gets a fresh deep copy. The old comment was accurate and the new one is wrong.

issues.summary: The same chainId assertion appears twice in the synthTxRequest test.
issues.label: nit
issues.evidence: walletConnectDappsSetup.test.ts:141 and :144 contain the identical `expect(request.params.chainId).toBe(...)`. It is harmless, redundant code.

issues.summary: The WcResponseIndicator tests never clear the outstanding request before responding, so they don't cover the same-tick clear that the ref was written for.
issues.label: low
issues.evidence: WcResponseIndicator.test.tsx:47-63 only dispatches setOutstandingRequest and then responds; nothing removes the entry. The comment at WcResponseIndicator.tsx:15-17 says the ref exists because the entry is cleared in the same tick, and a version computed during render would still pass these tests. The Maestro flows would still catch such a regression, so the impact is limited to the harness.

issues.summary: The Request-object branch of requestUrl, which is the one RTK fetchBaseQuery actually hits, has no unit test.
issues.label: low
issues.evidence: cgwClient.ts:53 uses fetchBaseQuery, which calls fetch with a Request, so proposeFetchMock.ts:23 (`input.url`) is the live path. proposeFetchMock.test.ts only passes string URLs. This is a real gap, but it is confined to the e2e harness.

issues.summary: A setupWcDappsTx failure is only sent to console.error, so Maestro flows go on and later fail with an unrelated symptom.
issues.label: low
issues.evidence: TestCtrls.e2e.tsx:343 swallows the rejection with `.catch(console.error)`, and no marker is exposed. The claim is valid, but it only affects how easy the harness is to debug.

issues.summary: Each happy/batch run adds a queued transaction to the shared staging Safe, and nothing ever cleans them up.
issues.label: low
issues.evidence: walletConnectDappsSetup.ts:60-69 adds jitter on purpose so every run proposes a new tx. The PR description admits the queue growth under 'Blast radius'. The risk is real but documented, and it only touches test infrastructure.

issues.summary: The final `text: 'Send'` assertion in the pending list is weak: a tx left over from an earlier run can satisfy it.
issues.label: low
issues.evidence: tx-send-happy.yml:96-97 asserts any 'Send' row. Queued txs from earlier runs accumulate on the Safe, so the step does not prove this run's tx was queued. The earlier hash-match marker (line 82-83) does cover delivery.

issues.summary: A comment still mentions 'the ticket's' CTA, although a commit in this PR removed ticket references.
issues.label: low
issues.evidence: tx-send-readonly-safe.yml:7-8 still says "the ticket's 'Add a signer' CTA", which the ticket-cleanup commit d12e9ebf1 missed. It is a minor documentation inconsistency.

issues.summary: The suite header still describes only pairing & session approval, but the suite now also runs management and tx-request flows.
issues.label: low
issues.evidence: __suite__.yml:6 reads 'pairing & session-approval suite', while the file now also runs manage-* and tx-send-* flows. This is a small documentation mismatch.

issues.summary: The claim that Object.keys insertion order is not guaranteed.
issues.label: wrong
issues.evidence: Since ES2015, Object.keys returns non-integer string keys in insertion order, and 0x… hashes are not integer-like. So taking the last key as the newest one at WcResponseIndicator.tsx:36 is well defined.

issues.summary: The claim that the install-once flag leaves the interceptor unhooked when Jest swaps global.fetch between suites.
issues.label: wrong
issues.evidence: Jest gives each test file its own module registry and global environment, so `installed` resets together with global.fetch. In the app, TestCtrls installs the mock once for the whole Metro lifetime, which is the documented intent (proposeFetchMock.ts:2).

issues.summary: A suggestion to document the install-once contract or add an uninstall function.
issues.label: nit
issues.evidence: proposeFetchMock.ts:2 already says it is 'Installed once from TestCtrls.e2e.tsx', and the test comment at line 12-13 explains the binding. No current consumer needs to uninstall it.

issues.summary: A hardcoded private key in the e2e setup.
issues.label: wrong
issues.evidence: The same throwaway Sepolia key was already committed before this PR, in apps/mobile/e2e/tests/onboarding/import-signer*.yml at the base commit, and walletConnectDappsSetup.ts:50-52 documents it as that public test key. It is an intentional, already-public test fixture, not a secret.

issues.summary: The useEffect without a dependency array runs on every render.
issues.label: nit
issues.evidence: WcResponseIndicator.tsx:34-38 does only a cheap ref write guarded by a length check. Running it on every render is correct, just slightly wasteful.

issues.summary: The batch bundle's chainId '0xaa36a7' is hardcoded instead of derived from the fixture.
issues.label: nit
issues.evidence: walletConnectDappsSetup.ts:81 hardcodes it, but walletConnectDappsSetup.test.ts:156 asserts that BigInt(bundle.chainId) equals mockedActiveAccount.chainId. A fixture change would therefore not break silently.

issues.summary: Owner and recipient addresses are duplicated as raw strings instead of reusing mockData.
issues.label: nit
issues.evidence: walletConnectDappsSetup.ts:53,73,85 repeat addresses that also appear in mockData.ts:23-24. Pulling them into shared constants would help maintenance, but nothing is broken today.

issues.summary: The 1x1 red marker style is duplicated from TestCtrls.
issues.label: nit
issues.evidence: WcResponseIndicator.tsx:65-71 matches the style in TestCtrls.e2e.tsx:389-393. It is a trivial style duplication with no real cost.

issues.summary: Timeout values are duplicated across the Maestro flows.
issues.label: nit
issues.evidence: Several flows repeat literals such as 30000 and 10000, as other suites in the repo do. This is a style preference.

issues.summary: The '.*0\.001.*' assertion could match several elements.
issues.label: nit
issues.evidence: assertVisible at tx-send-happy.yml:47-48 passes if any element matches, and all it is checking is that the amount is rendered on the confirm screen, which that is enough for.

issues.summary: A theoretical wei-jitter collision across module reloads.
issues.label: nit
issues.evidence: walletConnectDappsSetup.ts:68-69 combines Date.now() with a counter over a range of about 16.7M values. For sequential Maestro runs a collision is negligible, and even then it would only skip the sign tail.
